premise: What if the Moon vanished tonight?
why: A one-line premise everyone has wondered and nobody can film, with a huge visual moment (the Moon blinking out over a glowing blocky world) and real, checkable science behind every beat. It fits the 'aesthetic blocks' fantasy look: night sky, magic glow, sea, castle.
title: WHAT IF THE MOON VANISHED?

lines.text: What if the Moon vanished... tonight?
It hangs two hundred thirty-eight thousand miles away, and all that glow is borrowed sunlight.

facts.claim: The Moon is an average of 238,855 miles away.
facts.quote: The Moon is an average of 238,855 miles (384,400 kilometers) away.

lines.text: Then, in one blink... it's gone.
The Moon is the biggest pull on our tides. Without it, the seas fall back.

facts.claim: The Moon is the biggest influence on Earth's tides.
facts.quote: the Moon is the biggest influence on Earth's tides because of its proximity

lines.text: Only the Sun's tug is left, so the waves come back, smaller.

facts.claim: The Sun also makes tides; it partly cancels or adds to the Moon's.
facts.quote: the Sun's gravitational pull works against the Moon's gravitational tug and partially cancels it out

lines.text: Even Earth's slow wobble is driven by the Sun and the Moon. Lose one, and the spin changes its dance.

facts.claim: Earth's wobble (precession) is due to tidal forces from the Sun and Moon.
facts.quote: This wobble is due to tidal forces caused by the gravitational influences of the Sun and Moon

lines.text: Here's the twist. It's already leaving, about an inch and a half every year.

facts.claim: The Moon spirals away from Earth at about 1.5 inches (3.8 cm) a year.
facts.quote: the natural satellite slowly spirals away from Earth at a rate of about 1.5 inches (3.8 centimeters) per year

lines.text: So look up tonight. Say hi while it's still here.
